This reform transformed the network's governance by allowing TAO holders to freely choose which subnets they want to delegate their tokens to and participate in voting and reward allocation for the best subnets.\n\nHistorically, Bittensor's governance was centralized around the Root Subnet (Subnet 0), with only 64 validators responsible for distributing rewards. This system revealed several limitations: risk of manipulation, concentration of power, barriers to innovation, and a lack of transparency in the evaluation process.\n\nIt was within this context that the dTAO update emerged. Now, subnets have their own tokens (called alpha tokens) and compete to attract TAO from investors. This paradigm shift has two major effects:\n\n- It incentivizes teams to build robust projects with clear value propositions and effective communication;\n- It gives TAO holders an active role in the network's resource allocation, transforming Bittensor into a decentralized, market-driven incubator.\n\nEach user can now gain exposure to subnets by staking TAO tokens in them and receiving a subnet token in return, whose price fluctuates based on demand. This mechanism turns staking into a speculative bet. But how can one identify the most promising subnets in a sea of often technical, opaque, or very early-stage projects?\n\n→ Read our full presentation of Bittensor (TAO) :\n\nhttps://oakresearch.io/en/reports/protocols/bittensor-tao-presentation-protocol-combining-ai-blockchain\n\n---\n\n## How to Evaluate a Subnet?\n\nSince the dTAO update, the number of subnets on Bittensor has exploded. Currently, over 80 subnets are active, with projections exceeding 200 by year-end. With this exponential growth, it's essential to adopt a rigorous framework to evaluate a subnet's quality and potential.\n\nSeveral criteria can guide this analysis:\n\n**1. Project Fundamentals**\n\n- **Founding team**: A public, experienced team with backgrounds in AI, Web3, or reputable institutions is a strong signal. Subnets backed by solid entities (Macrocosmos, Rayon Labs, Inference Labs, etc.) have shown the ability to deliver quickly.\n- **Value proposition**: The product or service should solve a real problem. Projects with a clear, easily understandable mission have an edge in gaining market attention (e.g., deepfake detection, 3D generation, distributed training...).\n- **Addressable market**: Subnets targeting fast-growing verticals (compute, AI agents, AI x DePIN, healthcare, etc.) often show higher potential.\n\n**2. Narrative Attractiveness**\n\nIn the post-dTAO environment, it's no longer just technical validators allocating network resources, but the market itself. This means that storytelling, mindshare, and project clarity are just as critical as the technology—much like the rest of the crypto market.\n\n- **Clear narrative**: Projects that can explain what they do in one sentence have a strong advantage.\n- **Presence on X and Discord**: Active subnets that share updates, performance data, or integrations naturally attract more stakers.\n- **Design and UX**: A well-designed dashboard, app, or even a visual can spark enthusiasm.\n\n\u003e Example: Chutes gained visibility from a single well-shared comparison visual, while Tensorplex saw its token price skyrocket after an investment announcement from CZ's fund, even before the platform went live.\n\u003e \n\n**3. Real Traction**\n\nIf the goal of the network is to foster AI solutions with real-world usage, then user traction and monetization are fundamental indicators:\n\n- Number of users/downloads (e.g., Dippy, 4M+ users)\n- Revenue generated (e.g., Celium, $1M+ in 5 months)\n- Token utility within a clear economic model (buybacks, usage, etc.)\n\nHowever, these criteria need nuance. Some projects like Metanova or Safescan are still in the research phase, and their value will become apparent over time. Their contribution to Bittensor lies more in advancing research than in immediate revenue.\n\n**4. Other Signals**\n\nAdditional indicators can indirectly gauge a project's credibility:\n\n- Subnet mindshare within the community (tracked via tools like Swordscan).\n- Support from recognized investors or validators (e.g., Yuma, DCG's incubator branch; Crucible Labs, a top validator).\n- Attention from major validators (OpenTensor, Mentat Minds...), helping identify trending subnets.\n- Emission ranking (based on staker voting), which—if the market functions well—should favor the most promising subnets with higher staker interest and emissions.\n\nFor deeper insights, Bittensor’s Discord often offers more valuable information than Twitter or official websites.\n\n→ Read our full analysis of Bittensor's Dynamic TAO (dTAO) update :\n\nhttps://oakresearch.io/en/analyses/fundamentals/bittensor-tao-dynamic-tao-dtao-upgrade-changes-everything\n\n---\n\n## Subnet Mapping\n\nTo bring more clarity to the over 80 subnets now live on the Bittensor network, we've created a [Notion board](https://www.notion.so/1b52bfcc058180e890aceedb7ed12003?pvs=21) compiled by our contributor Victor. It features detailed entries for each subnet, with short descriptions, key links (website, X, GitHub), application status, and most importantly, a tier-based ranking from S (most promising) to D (least promising). This ranking is updated regularly based on traction, real progress, and community sentiment.\n\nIn this section, we present a curated selection of 25 subnets that we currently consider the most promising to follow. This is not financial advice, but a starting point for refining your own research.\n\n![ecosystem-mapping-bittensor.webp](https://assets.oakresearch.io/ecosystem_mapping_bittensor_757dd075f7.webp)\n\n- **Apex (SN1)**\n\nRun by Macrocosmos, Apex is one of the most advanced subnets in AI model inference. It incentivizes miners to build workflows that optimize conversational agents. The app is live with multiple models available.\n\n- **Omron (SN2)**\n\nA subnet focused on zero-knowledge proof of inference (zkML). Led by Inference Labs, one of the most technically proficient teams. Already integrated into several projects. Massive potential for decentralized AI.\n\n- **Templar (SN3)**\n\nIn a transitional phase, Templar is a pioneer in distributed AI model training. Personally recommended by Const (Bittensor founder), making it worth watching despite a limited web presence.\n\n- **Targon (SN4)**\n\nDeveloped by Manifold Labs, Targon aims to make inference faster and cheaper. Outperforms Web2 solutions on some benchmarks and offers an accessible playground with multiple open-source models.\n\n- **OpenKaito (SN5)**\n\nBacked by Kaito, a major player in InfoFi. Still early, building around text embedding models. Worth watching, especially with upcoming Yaps integrations.\n\n- **Infinite Game (SN6)**\n\nA creative concept based on event prediction. Building an AI agent (Aion) to guide decision-making on platforms like Polymarket. Strong narrative, execution still to be proven.\n\n- **Proprietary Trading Network (SN8)**\n\nDeveloped by Taoshi with a quantitative trading focus. Miners compete to deliver the best trading signals. Glitch Financial app is in beta. Execution looks serious.\n\n- **Pre-training (SN9)**\n\nAnother Macrocosmos subnet focused on foundation model training. Goal: create top-tier open-source pre-trained models for fine-tuning via the network.\n\n- **Dippy Roleplay (SN11)**\n\nA consumer-facing subnet focused on roleplay AI. High traction: 4M+ users, top 3 in Germany’s App Store, token buybacks. Great product execution and strong commercial strategy.\n\n- **Data Universe (SN13)**\n\nAlso from Macrocosmos, this subnet focuses on dataset collection and sharing. Functional app already scrapes and visualizes data. A key link in the network’s AI pipeline.\n\n- **404 GEN (SN17)**\n\nFormerly a Web2 company (Atlas), now focused on 3D content generation via AI. Smooth migration to Bittensor. One-click 3D generation app live. Clear use case in gaming.\n\n- **Nineteen (SN19)**\n\nFirst subnet from Rayon Labs. Optimizes inference on models like Llama 3.1. Outperforms Web2 competitors with lower costs and open API. Solid app, methodical approach.\n\n- **Protein Folding (SN25)**\n\nA scientific project by Macrocosmos simulating protein folding for biomedical research. Over 160,000 folded proteins. University collaborations. High-potential DeSci use case.\n\n- **It’s AI (SN32)**\n\nDetects AI-generated content. Functional app analyzes documents and text. Accessible narrative, rapidly growing market. Strong potential for mass adoption.\n\n- **Bitmind (SN34)**\n\nSpecialist in deepfake detection. Trusted team with strong community roots. Browser extension already live. Clear value proposition, well-executed.\n\n- **Fine-tuning (SN37)**\n\nThe final component of Macrocosmos’s AI pipeline. Hosts fine-tuning competitions to optimize models for specific use cases. Technical and gamified approach.\n\n- **Masa (SN42)**\n\nWeb3-native project specializing in real-time data scraping (X, Telegram, Discord). Subnet 42 logged over 320M data points—more than X’s own API. Strong use case, integrations in progress.\n\n- **Score Vision (SN44)**\n\nApplies computer vision to football. Uses match footage for analysis, betting, or AI agent training. Working with CrunchDAO. Unique product.\n\n- **Synth (SN50)**\n\nBuilt by Mode Network, Synth uses synthetic data to forecast price movements—currently focused on BTC. Strong narrative, execution underway.\n\n- **Celium (SN51)**\n\nGPU marketplace on Bittensor. Over $1M in revenue in 5 months. Endorsed by Const and OpenTensor Foundation. A prime example of DePIN: useful and profitable.\n\n- **Dojo (SN52)**\n\nTensorplex subnet for human data collection. Platform not yet live, but recent investment from CZ’s fund sent the token soaring. Execution to be monitored.\n\n- **Gradients (SN56)**\n\nSecond Rayon Labs subnet, focused on no-code AI. Lets users train models with zero technical skills. In beta, but UI is very intuitive. Could broaden Bittensor’s user base.\n\n- **Chutes (SN64)**\n\nThird subnet from Rayon Labs, providing GPUs for general-purpose inference. Over 12M tokens processed daily. Strong integration with Rayon’s AI agent. Solid tech, good storytelling.\n\n- **Nova (SN68)**\n\nCreated by Metanova, focused on drug discovery. Simulates chemical compounds to identify therapeutic molecules. Strong DeSci narrative. Semi-anonymous team but actively building.\n\n- **Safescan (SN76)**\n\nRecently revived project aiming to detect cancer using AI. Ambitious, still in R\u0026D. Long-term subnet, but with one of the most powerful narratives if successful.\n\n---\n\n## How to Invest in a Subnet\n\nThe introduction of alpha tokens has turned staking on Bittensor into a genuine speculative market. Each subnet now has its own token, whose price currently fluctuates based on various parameters. This mechanism allows for direct exposure to the perceived performance of the subnet, but also introduces significant volatility and risk.\n\nToday, most subnet tokens are highly illiquid, with low market caps, aggressive emissions, and a high degree of speculation. It’s common to see some tokens gain +300% in a single day, only to drop -90% shortly after. Investing in a subnet means betting on a team, a vision, an execution—but also on its ability to market itself effectively in a competitive and immature environment.\n\nIn this context, several staking strategies are available for TAO holders.\n\n**1. The Conservative Approach: Staking on the Root Subnet (SN0)**\n\nThis is the simplest and least risky strategy: staking your TAO on subnet 0 provides a stable yield without exposure to the volatility of subnet tokens. The yield decreases over time, but it remains attractive—especially compared to the risks elsewhere on the network. It’s the default option for those who want to participate in the ecosystem without analyzing each project individually.\n\n**2. Delegation via Mentat Minds**\n\nFor those who want to optimize their yield without dedicating too much time, Mentat Minds offers a simple, non-custodial, and secure solution, made possible by Substrate infrastructure. Three strategies are currently available:\n\n- *Optimized Root*: staking only on SN0, automatically selecting the best-performing validators.\n- *Protected Alpha*: same principle, but dividends are reinvested in top 15 subnet tokens. The initial capital is never exposed—only the yield is.\n- *Alpha 5*: a more aggressive strategy where 100% of TAO is exposed to subnet tokens from the top 5. High potential returns, but also a risk of capital loss if selected tokens drop.\n\nMentat Minds allows you to delegate TAO at any time, with no unstaking period and no loss of control over your wallet thanks to the proxy system. It is currently one of the most robust solutions for TAO holders.\n\n\u003e To join Mentat Minds, [here's an affiliate link proposed by Victor.crypto](https://www.mentatminds.com/delegate/?origin=victor_crypto), feel free to use it to support his work.\n\u003e \n\n**3. The Active Approach: Manually Selecting Subnets**\n\nThis approach consists of analyzing subnets individually to choose where to stake your TAO. It is the most time-consuming method but also potentially the most rewarding—provided you have strong risk management and can read subtle signals effectively.\n\nSince subnet tokens face high selling pressure (due to emissions), only projects capable of generating real traction—or attracting significant community attention—manage to hold up over time. It is crucial to diversify, monitor subnet developments (Discord, X, roadmap), and be ready to adjust allocations.\n\n\nSome tips if you choose this approach:\n\n- Invest only a small portion of your TAO in the most promising subnets.\n- Avoid overly opaque subnets or those whose tokens have already done a 5x without any tangible announcement.\n- Favor projects with real user traction or demonstrable short-term utility.\n- Stay active on Discord: valuable insights often circulate there well before X or official announcements.45:[\"$\",\"$L4e\",null,{\"locale\":\"en\",\"post\":{\"id\":1775,\"documentId\":\"fp103jd0rudcrkko4nc16nus\",\"title\":\"Bittensor subnets: The best opportunities for investing in TAO\",\"slug\":\"bittensor-subnets-best-opportunities-investing-tao\",\"locale\":\"en\",\"type\":\"innovations\",\"content\":\"$4f\",\"introduction\":\"Bittensor has experienced tremendous growth since the launch of the Dynamic TAO upgrade. <p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">In February 2024, the Bittensor protocol underwent one of the most significant upgrades in its history: Dynamic TAO (dTAO). This reform transformed the network's governance by allowing TAO holders to freely choose which subnets they want to delegate their tokens to and participate in voting and reward allocation for the best subnets.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Historically, Bittensor's governance was centralized around the Root Subnet (Subnet 0), with only 64 validators responsible for distributing rewards. This system revealed several limitations: risk of manipulation, concentration of power, barriers to innovation, and a lack of transparency in the evaluation process.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">It was within this context that the dTAO update emerged. Now, subnets have their own tokens (called alpha tokens) and compete to attract TAO from investors. This paradigm shift has two major effects:</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">It incentivizes teams to build robust projects with clear value propositions and effective communication;</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">It gives TAO holders an active role in the network's resource allocation, transforming Bittensor into a decentralized, market-driven incubator.</li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Each user can now gain exposure to subnets by staking TAO tokens in them and receiving a subnet token in return, whose price fluctuates based on demand. This mechanism turns staking into a speculative bet. But how can one identify the most promising subnets in a sea of often technical, opaque, or very early-stage projects?</p>

<h2 class="text-3xl pt-8 pb-4 font-bold" id="how-to-evaluate-a-subnet" node="[object Object]">How to Evaluate a Subnet?</h2>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Since the dTAO update, the number of subnets on Bittensor has exploded. Currently, over 80 subnets are active, with projections exceeding 200 by year-end. With this exponential growth, it's essential to adopt a rigorous framework to evaluate a subnet's quality and potential.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Several criteria can guide this analysis:</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg"><strong>1. Project Fundamentals</strong></p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Founding team</strong>: A public, experienced team with backgrounds in AI, Web3, or reputable institutions is a strong signal. Subnets backed by solid entities (Macrocosmos, Rayon Labs, Inference Labs, etc.) have shown the ability to deliver quickly.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Value proposition</strong>: The product or service should solve a real problem. Projects with a clear, easily understandable mission have an edge in gaining market attention (e.g., deepfake detection, 3D generation, distributed training...).</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Addressable market</strong>: Subnets targeting fast-growing verticals (compute, AI agents, AI x DePIN, healthcare, etc.) often show higher potential.</li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg"><strong>2. Narrative Attractiveness</strong></p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">In the post-dTAO environment, it's no longer just technical validators allocating network resources, but the market itself. This means that storytelling, mindshare, and project clarity are just as critical as the technology-much like the rest of the crypto market.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Clear narrative</strong>: Projects that can explain what they do in one sentence have a strong advantage.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Presence on X and Discord</strong>: Active subnets that share updates, performance data, or integrations naturally attract more stakers.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Design and UX</strong>: A well-designed dashboard, app, or even a visual can spark enthusiasm.</li>
</ul>
<blockquote class="my-4 border-primary border-l-4 pl-4 italic" node="[object Object]">
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Example: Chutes gained visibility from a single well-shared comparison visual, while Tensorplex saw its token price skyrocket after an investment announcement from CZ's fund, even before the platform went live.</p>
</blockquote>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg"><strong>3. Real Traction</strong></p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">If the goal of the network is to foster AI solutions with real-world usage, then user traction and monetization are fundamental indicators:</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Number of users/downloads (e.g., Dippy, 4M+ users)</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Revenue generated (e.g., Celium, $1M+ in 5 months)</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Token utility within a clear economic model (buybacks, usage, etc.)</li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">However, these criteria need nuance. Some projects like Metanova or Safescan are still in the research phase, and their value will become apparent over time. Their contribution to Bittensor lies more in advancing research than in immediate revenue.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg"><strong>4. Other Signals</strong></p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Additional indicators can indirectly gauge a project's credibility:</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Subnet mindshare within the community (tracked via tools like Swordscan).</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Support from recognized investors or validators (e.g., Yuma, DCG's incubator branch; Crucible Labs, a top validator).</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Attention from major validators (OpenTensor, Mentat Minds...), helping identify trending subnets.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Emission ranking (based on staker voting), which-if the market functions well-should favor the most promising subnets with higher staker interest and emissions.</li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">For deeper insights, Bittensor’s Discord often offers more valuable information than Twitter or official websites.</p>

<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">In this section, we present a curated selection of 25 subnets that we currently consider the most promising to follow. This is not financial advice, but a starting point for refining your own research.</p>

<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Apex (SN1)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Run by Macrocosmos, Apex is one of the most advanced subnets in AI model inference. It incentivizes miners to build workflows that optimize conversational agents. The app is live with multiple models available.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Omron (SN2)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">A subnet focused on zero-knowledge proof of inference (zkML). Led by Inference Labs, one of the most technically proficient teams. Already integrated into several projects. Massive potential for decentralized AI.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Templar (SN3)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">In a transitional phase, Templar is a pioneer in distributed AI model training. Personally recommended by Const (Bittensor founder), making it worth watching despite a limited web presence.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Targon (SN4)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Developed by Manifold Labs, Targon aims to make inference faster and cheaper. Outperforms Web2 solutions on some benchmarks and offers an accessible playground with multiple open-source models.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>OpenKaito (SN5)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Backed by Kaito, a major player in InfoFi. Still early, building around text embedding models. Worth watching, especially with upcoming Yaps integrations.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Infinite Game (SN6)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">A creative concept based on event prediction. Building an AI agent (Aion) to guide decision-making on platforms like Polymarket. Strong narrative, execution still to be proven.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Proprietary Trading Network (SN8)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Developed by Taoshi with a quantitative trading focus. Miners compete to deliver the best trading signals. Glitch Financial app is in beta. Execution looks serious.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Pre-training (SN9)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Another Macrocosmos subnet focused on foundation model training. Goal: create top-tier open-source pre-trained models for fine-tuning via the network.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Dippy Roleplay (SN11)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">A consumer-facing subnet focused on roleplay AI. High traction: 4M+ users, top 3 in Germany’s App Store, token buybacks. Great product execution and strong commercial strategy.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Data Universe (SN13)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Also from Macrocosmos, this subnet focuses on dataset collection and sharing. Functional app already scrapes and visualizes data. A key link in the network’s AI pipeline.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>404 GEN (SN17)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Formerly a Web2 company (Atlas), now focused on 3D content generation via AI. Smooth migration to Bittensor. One-click 3D generation app live. Clear use case in gaming.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Nineteen (SN19)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">First subnet from Rayon Labs. Optimizes inference on models like Llama 3.1. Outperforms Web2 competitors with lower costs and open API. Solid app, methodical approach.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Protein Folding (SN25)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">A scientific project by Macrocosmos simulating protein folding for biomedical research. Over 160,000 folded proteins. University collaborations. High-potential DeSci use case.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>It’s AI (SN32)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Detects AI-generated content. Functional app analyzes documents and text. Accessible narrative, rapidly growing market. Strong potential for mass adoption.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Bitmind (SN34)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Specialist in deepfake detection. Trusted team with strong community roots. Browser extension already live. Clear value proposition, well-executed.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Fine-tuning (SN37)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">The final component of Macrocosmos’s AI pipeline. Hosts fine-tuning competitions to optimize models for specific use cases. Technical and gamified approach.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Masa (SN42)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Web3-native project specializing in real-time data scraping (X, Telegram, Discord). Subnet 42 logged over 320M data points-more than X’s own API. Strong use case, integrations in progress.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Score Vision (SN44)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Applies computer vision to football. Uses match footage for analysis, betting, or AI agent training. Working with CrunchDAO. Unique product.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Synth (SN50)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Built by Mode Network, Synth uses synthetic data to forecast price movements-currently focused on BTC. Strong narrative, execution underway.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Celium (SN51)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">GPU marketplace on Bittensor. Over $1M in revenue in 5 months. Endorsed by Const and OpenTensor Foundation. A prime example of DePIN: useful and profitable.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Dojo (SN52)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Tensorplex subnet for human data collection. Platform not yet live, but recent investment from CZ’s fund sent the token soaring. Execution to be monitored.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Gradients (SN56)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Second Rayon Labs subnet, focused on no-code AI. Lets users train models with zero technical skills. In beta, but UI is very intuitive. Could broaden Bittensor’s user base.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Chutes (SN64)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Third subnet from Rayon Labs, providing GPUs for general-purpose inference. Over 12M tokens processed daily. Strong integration with Rayon’s AI agent. Solid tech, good storytelling.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Nova (SN68)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Created by Metanova, focused on drug discovery. Simulates chemical compounds to identify therapeutic molecules. Strong DeSci narrative. Semi-anonymous team but actively building.</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><strong>Safescan (SN76)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Recently revived project aiming to detect cancer using AI. Ambitious, still in R&D. Long-term subnet, but with one of the most powerful narratives if successful.</p>
<hr class="my-8 border-border" node="[object Object]">
<h2 class="text-3xl pt-8 pb-4 font-bold" id="how-to-invest-in-a-subnet" node="[object Object]">How to Invest in a Subnet</h2>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">The introduction of alpha tokens has turned staking on Bittensor into a genuine speculative market. Each subnet now has its own token, whose price currently fluctuates based on various parameters. This mechanism allows for direct exposure to the perceived performance of the subnet, but also introduces significant volatility and risk.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Today, most subnet tokens are highly illiquid, with low market caps, aggressive emissions, and a high degree of speculation. It’s common to see some tokens gain +300% in a single day, only to drop -90% shortly after. Investing in a subnet means betting on a team, a vision, an execution-but also on its ability to market itself effectively in a competitive and immature environment.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">In this context, several staking strategies are available for TAO holders.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg"><strong>1. The Conservative Approach: Staking on the Root Subnet (SN0)</strong></p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">This is the simplest and least risky strategy: staking your TAO on subnet 0 provides a stable yield without exposure to the volatility of subnet tokens. The yield decreases over time, but it remains attractive-especially compared to the risks elsewhere on the network. It’s the default option for those who want to participate in the ecosystem without analyzing each project individually.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg"><strong>2. Delegation via Mentat Minds</strong></p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">For those who want to optimize their yield without dedicating too much time, Mentat Minds offers a simple, non-custodial, and secure solution, made possible by Substrate infrastructure. Three strategies are currently available:</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><em>Optimized Root</em>: staking only on SN0, automatically selecting the best-performing validators.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><em>Protected Alpha</em>: same principle, but dividends are reinvested in top 15 subnet tokens. The initial capital is never exposed-only the yield is.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]"><em>Alpha 5</em>: a more aggressive strategy where 100% of TAO is exposed to subnet tokens from the top 5. High potential returns, but also a risk of capital loss if selected tokens drop.</li>
</ul>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Mentat Minds allows you to delegate TAO at any time, with no unstaking period and no loss of control over your wallet thanks to the proxy system. It is currently one of the most robust solutions for TAO holders.</p>
<blockquote class="my-4 border-primary border-l-4 pl-4 italic" node="[object Object]">
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">To join Mentat Minds, <a class="text-primary hover:underline" href="https://www.mentatminds.com/delegate/?origin=victor_crypto" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" node="[object Object]">here's an affiliate link proposed by Victor.crypto</a>, feel free to use it to support his work.</p>
</blockquote>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg"><strong>3. The Active Approach: Manually Selecting Subnets</strong></p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">This approach consists of analyzing subnets individually to choose where to stake your TAO. It is the most time-consuming method but also potentially the most rewarding-provided you have strong risk management and can read subtle signals effectively.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Since subnet tokens face high selling pressure (due to emissions), only projects capable of generating real traction-or attracting significant community attention-manage to hold up over time. It is crucial to diversify, monitor subnet developments (Discord, X, roadmap), and be ready to adjust allocations.</p>
<p class="mb-5 font-normal text-lg">Some tips if you choose this approach:</p>
<ul class="mb-4 list-disc pl-6" node="[object Object]">
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Invest only a small portion of your TAO in the most promising subnets.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Avoid overly opaque subnets or those whose tokens have already done a 5x without any tangible announcement.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Favor projects with real user traction or demonstrable short-term utility.</li>
<li class="my-2 font-medium text-base" node="[object Object]">Stay active on Discord: valuable insights often circulate there well before X or official announcements.</li>
